# Technical Requirements for "Virtual Machine RTOS Shall Work as Expected"

This is a common challenge in ISO 26262 — decomposing a high-level (and vaguely stated) functional requirement into verifiable **technical safety requirements**. Below is a structured breakdown of the kinds of technical requirements you would typically derive, organized by key aspects of RTOS behavior in a virtualized/hypervisor environment.

---

## 1. Temporal Determinism / Scheduling

| ID | Technical Requirement |
|---|---|
| TR-01 | The VM RTOS shall meet all task deadlines as defined by its scheduling policy (e.g., worst-case execution time bounds) |
| TR-02 | The hypervisor shall guarantee a minimum CPU time allocation to the RTOS VM within each scheduling period (e.g., ≥ X ms every Y ms) |
| TR-03 | Interrupt latency for the RTOS VM shall not exceed a defined maximum (e.g., ≤ Z µs) |
| TR-04 | Jitter on periodic tasks within the RTOS VM shall remain within specified bounds |
| TR-05 | The hypervisor shall ensure temporal isolation — other VMs shall not impact the RTOS VM's timing behavior |

---

## 2. Spatial Isolation / Memory Protection

| ID | Technical Requirement |
|---|---|
| TR-06 | The hypervisor shall enforce memory isolation between the RTOS VM and all other VMs |
| TR-07 | The RTOS VM shall only access memory regions explicitly assigned to it |
| TR-08 | Any unauthorized memory access attempt shall be detected and reported (or trapped) by the hypervisor |
| TR-09 | The RTOS shall maintain integrity of its internal data structures (stack, heap, task control blocks) |

---

## 3. Startup & Initialization

| ID | Technical Requirement |
|---|---|
| TR-10 | The RTOS VM shall complete initialization within a defined maximum time (e.g., ≤ T ms after power-on) |
| TR-11 | The RTOS shall verify the integrity of its own image (e.g., CRC/checksum) before entering operational mode |
| TR-12 | The RTOS shall reach a defined "ready" state and signal availability to other system components |

---

## 4. Execution Integrity / Correct Operation

| ID | Technical Requirement |
|---|---|
| TR-13 | All RTOS tasks shall execute in the correct order and priority as defined by the system configuration |
| TR-14 | Inter-process communication (IPC) mechanisms shall deliver messages without corruption, loss, or duplication |
| TR-15 | Shared resources shall be protected by appropriate synchronization mechanisms (mutexes, semaphores) without deadlock |
| TR-16 | The RTOS shall handle all configured interrupts and route them to the correct ISR |

---

## 5. Error Detection & Handling

| ID | Technical Requirement |
|---|---|
| TR-17 | The RTOS shall implement an alive/heartbeat mechanism detectable by an external safety monitor |
| TR-18 | The RTOS shall detect task deadline violations (watchdog or deadline monitoring) |
| TR-19 | Stack overflow for any task shall be detected and a defined error response shall be triggered |
| TR-20 | The RTOS shall enter a defined safe state upon detection of an unrecoverable internal error |
| TR-21 | The RTOS shall log/report detected errors via a diagnostic interface |

---

## 6. Freedom from Interference (FFI)

| ID | Technical Requirement |
|---|---|
| TR-22 | The RTOS VM shall not interfere with higher-ASIL or other safety-relevant VMs (temporal and spatial) |
| TR-23 | Communication between VMs shall be mediated by the hypervisor with defined access control and data validation |
| TR-24 | Resource consumption (CPU, memory, I/O bandwidth) by the RTOS VM shall be bounded and monitored |

---

## 7. Configuration & Deterministic Behavior

| ID | Technical Requirement |
|---|---|
| TR-25 | The RTOS configuration (task set, priorities, stack sizes, scheduling parameters) shall be statically defined and verified at build time |
| TR-26 | Dynamic memory allocation during runtime shall be prohibited (or constrained to a pre-allocated pool) |
| TR-27 | The RTOS behavior shall be reproducible (deterministic) under identical input conditions |

---

## 8. Shutdown & Reset

| ID | Technical Requirement |
|---|---|
| TR-28 | The RTOS VM shall support a controlled shutdown sequence upon request |
| TR-29 | Upon reset, the RTOS VM shall return to a known, safe initial state |
| TR-30 | The RTOS shall be capable of being reset independently of other VMs (if required by the safety concept) |

---

## Key ISO 26262 Considerations

- **ASIL Decomposition**: If the RTOS VM supports a safety function, each technical requirement must be allocated an appropriate ASIL level (Part 9 — ASIL decomposition may apply across VMs).
- **Dependent Failure Analysis (DFA)**: Requires evidence of freedom from interference — especially Part 6, Clause 7 and Part 9.
- **Verification**: Each technical requirement must be verifiable through **testing, analysis, simulation, or review** (Part 6, Clause 9 / Part 8).
- **Traceability**: Each technical requirement must trace back to the functional requirement and forward to design, implementation, and test cases.

---

## Recommendation

The original functional requirement *"VM RTOS shall work as expected"* is **not well-formed** per ISO 26262 standards — it is ambiguous, not measurable, and not verifiable. It should be refined into multiple **specific, measurable, and testable** functional safety requirements before decomposition into technical requirements. The above gives you a starting framework for that decomposition.
